name: Rochdale member consumer cooperative
description: The Rochdale Equitable Pioneers established a member-owned consumer store, financing its opening through subscriptions and loans; its later cooperative model combined equal voting, member dividends and education.

date.label: 21 December 1844
date.basis: The Co-operative Heritage Trust dates the store’s opening to 21 December 1844.

events.statement: Members opened their cooperative store in Rochdale.
events.caveats: The heritage account describes a set of principles without establishing the precise implementation date of each. Cooperatives existed before Rochdale; equal voting and open membership must not be read as evidence that all residents could afford to join.

evidence.supports: Members opened their cooperative store in Rochdale.

events.scope: Opening of one member consumer society in Rochdale, rather than the origin of cooperatives in general.

contributions.group: Original members of the Rochdale Equitable Pioneers Society
contributions.resource: Raised money through subscriptions and loans to rent a shop.

evidence.supports: The heritage account identifies subscriptions and loans as funding the rent.

contributions.group: Pioneer purchasers John Holt and David Brooks
contributions.resource: Were appointed to purchase stock for opening night.

evidence.supports: Names Holt and Brooks as the purchasers appointed 12 December 1844.

events.population: Original society members and customers served by the Rochdale shop

earliest_record.rationale: The Co-operative Heritage Trust dates the store’s opening to 21 December 1844. Earliest record means earliest currently established for this scoped case, not global priority.

caveats: The heritage account describes a set of principles without establishing the precise implementation date of each. Cooperatives existed before Rochdale; equal voting and open membership must not be read as evidence that all residents could afford to join.

research.note: The underlying event and domain were independently checked in an earlier pass. Place, scope and contributions were added in a subsequent sourcing pass and have not been independently checked; event basis is sourced to reflect the new additions.

measures.conditions: Storefront rental agreed by founding members in Rochdale in 1844, as reported by the Co-operative Heritage Trust; nominal historical currency.

evidence.supports: The account reports rent of £10 per year.

measures.conditions: Working-class men described by the Co-operative Heritage Trust as establishing the Rochdale consumer society; not a count of all subsequent members.

evidence.supports: The account states that 28 working-class men came together to establish the society.
